idiom_name: hand-rolled ring buffer + pthread mutex/condition variable (or POSIX mq_*)
implementation_notes: C ships no queue abstraction, so the classic structure is written by hand: a fixed-capacity array with head/tail indices taken modulo the capacity, a pthread_mutex_t guarding both, and a pthread_cond_t whose wait loop suspends the drain thread until an item arrives (pthread_cond_wait/pthread_cond_signal with the predicate re-checked under the lock). When the events cross a process boundary, the kernel can own the queue instead: POSIX mq_open/mq_send/mq_receive give a named bounded queue with mq_notify for asynchronous arrival, at the cost of byte-sized messages, priority ordering and kernel persistence. The hand-rolled form is still justified whenever the payload is typed data and the queue must stay allocation-free.
pitfalls: A full ring buffer must not overwrite unread entries: (tail + 1) % N == head means full - decide block/drop/coalesce there instead of asserting only in debug builds.
pthread_cond_wait must be called with the mutex held and re-test the predicate in a loop; a signal raised between unlock and wait is lost, and pthread_cond_signal is not async-signal-safe.
POSIX mq_* messages are byte strings delivered highest-priority-first rather than plain FIFO, and the queue persists in the kernel until mq_unlink - neither matches an in-process typed FIFO.
